Verdict: Strong Hire.

# LLD Round
Design a data structure with time-to-live (TTL) where you receive (key, timestamp) pairs (in increasing order). You need to provide:
a) Count of all active keys
b) Count of active keys for a particular key
c) CRUD functions

Approach: Map<String, Queue<Timestamp>>. At every function call, go through the map and remove expired keys. Also maintain global counters.

This approach worked, but the interviewer wanted something like a Queue<Pair> where Pair = (timestamp, key). This way, instead of iterating over the map for every key, we can directly poll elements from the queue irrespective of the key, and update counts using Map<String, Integer> and a global totalCounter. The worst-case complexity is the same, but this is simpler and has better average-case complexity.

Verdict: Lean Hire.

Design a recommendation system for the Amazon homepage.

Approach: I converted this into a Top-K problem where I was tracking metrics like item view count and item buy count in Flink, then maintaining sorted sets and using these sets to get recommendations in real time.

title: Design a Logging System

sources.passage:
I totally bombed. They asked to design ranged key-value storage with three operations: get(key), set(key, value), getRange(startKey, endKey) in concurrent, multithreaded environment. They wanted me to optimize locking mechanism to reduce wait time and deadlock situation (e.g. when getRange is getting called, only lock those range for set operation.)

I couldn't solve the problem because I had zero knowledge about concurrency. Interviewer later went over the solution using [synchonized](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/essential/concurrency/syncmeth.html) keyword, [Semaphore](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/Semaphore.html), [Runnable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Runnable.html), and some kind of callback function but I didn't understand a single thing.

Shouldn't they at least tell me that I should prepare for concurrency? How am I supposed to know that I should be familiar with them?

**Round 3: Beavioral**
Just standard behavioral round. Looks like it went well. no red flags.

**Round 4: System Design**
This is another round that didn't go well. They asked me to design a logging system. I followed the structure similar to HelloInterview, and proposed high-level design including write-heavy database (for write) and inverted index (for query). They asked a lot of follow-up questions failure scenarios, in which I answered by throwing more stuffs to diagram (e.g. horizontal scaling, cron job reconcilation, alerting). The feedback I got is that high-level design was good, but didn't handle failure scenarios well.
